texts: Left ventricular distension on weaning after a mitral repair with a complete ring is most likely caused by a ring stitch that has caught the non-coronary cusp of the aortic valve, producing acute aortic regurgitation.
The anterior mitral annulus lies right next to the aortic valve along the aorto-mitral curtain, and stitches placed there can bite an aortic cusp.
Intraoperative TEE shows the new aortic regurgitation, and the offending stitch must be removed and replaced.
Air in the right coronary artery affects the right ventricle, an injured circumflex causes a lateral wall motion defect, and an atrioventricular disruption causes bleeding.
In the picture, a stitch of the new brass ring holds the orca's plain back lip open, and water pours back into the swelling red room.
Memory hook: a mitral ring stitch that bites the orca's lip floods the red room.
